design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (insurance_rejections_and_prior_auth, category coverage).

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: {"task": 1, "key": "env_0021_retail_pharmacy_chain/insurance_rejections_and_prior_auth/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}. Tree: 1 prerequisite problem; root and prerequisite each take 6 factors.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: coverage_ext_appeal_decision_window (file_coverage_appeal_f21a07b8) and coverage_ext_continuation_supply_days (bill_continuation_supply_837ca024) - appeals and continuation supplies on the prior-authorization side. Claimed now, disjoint: coverage_ext_corrected_rebill_patient_pay (rebill_corrected_claim_b015fa67, agent, state_due) and coverage_ext_cash_rebill_patient_pay (submit_cash_fill_rebill_483f3c39, user, on_request) - re-billing on the claim side. This is the last task (M = 2); after it the four extended policies are covered once each. Owner note: the blueprint's owner=user writes are an appeal (taken by task 0) and removing an active plan, which records no quantity a policy could compute; the customer's own write here is the patient's submission of his own cash purchase for re-billing - his money and his decision to send a privately paid fill to his plan - handed over by the agent and run by him.

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks only to put a cash purchase through his new plan. The re-bill's patient pay is not fixed until every billing-correction reversal on the coverage is named by a re-billed claim (prerequisite sentence), and the ledger shows the 2026-09-17 lisinopril claim reversed on 2026-09-21 with nothing naming it. The agent must compute and book that corrected claim first (6 factors over the rx fill ledger, the claim ledger, the plan dates and the delivery product), then compute the cash re-bill (6 factors whose base rate is read from the corrected claim just written, plus the plan dates, the cash fills and the re-billed prescription's handling class) and hand it to the patient. The patient never mentions the lisinopril claim.

[Design thesis] surface goal ("put ... through your new work insurance") -> prerequisite (corrected claim naming the billing-correction reversal) -> core computation (cash re-bill patient_pay_usd) -> terminal state: two retro_rebill paid claims (4.32 corrected, 1.52 re-billed cash fill).

[Problem-tree card] root coverage_ext_cash_rebill_patient_pay; edge -> coverage_ext_corrected_rebill_patient_pay, kind value_input, gate rebill_rate, form state, prerequisite sentence: "The patient pay of a re-billed cash fill is not fixed until every claim on the coverage reversed for a billing correction is named by a re-billed claim on the claim ledger." Four-point test: (1) negated direction "not fixed until" (the way a billing desk says a charge waits), rewritable as "is fixed only after every such claim is named by a re-billed claim" with the same scope; the charter now carries both directions (task 0's sentence is affirmative "only after"); (2) XX is a record-visible state (a re-billed claim naming each billing-correction reversal); (3) no tool, id or snake_case token; (4) "every claim ... reversed for a billing correction" - the exact scope of the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings it about: only rebill_corrected_claim_b015fa67 records source_claim_id on a retro_rebill claim (the cash re-bill tool does not). Derivation: sentence + ledger (reversal 21b9c62c-1e24-44e8-974a-a88cd4e03212 names 7d5645e6-65ae-4b9f-ad50-3fcd249f04c4, no claim names it) + the corrected-claim rule ("is owed a corrected claim ... the corrected claim names the reversed claim") -> the corrected claim. Owner of the resolving write: agent; owner of the root: user. False at frozen_time: initial_state.coverage_claims.21b9c62c-1e24-44e8-974a-a88cd4e03212.reversal_reason = billing_correction, no paid row carries source_claim_id = 7d5645e6-65ae-4b9f-ad50-3fcd249f04c4. Order: corrected claim (step 12) then cash re-bill (step 14). Deletion run: skipping the corrected claim gives rebill_rate 0, member share 1 and patient pay 0.00 instead of 1.52. user_scenario names no prerequisite; tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] Both writes have subject coverage_claim_paid; governing base policies and gates: coverage_evt_claim_billing.bill_active_coverage_only (the Commercial Copay Plan 7ff87556-1ba1-4074-b6c6-1b297654ccb2 is active - satisfied); coverage_evt_refill_too_soon.plan_refill_date (time, anchor previous paid claim of the prescription, 80 percent: lisinopril 2026-08-20 + 22 = 2026-09-11 <= DOS 2026-09-17; atorvastatin 2026-08-13 + 22 = 2026-09-04 <= DOS 2026-09-12 - satisfied; one day earlier would be refill_too_soon); coverage_evt_claim_reversal.cash_rebill_window (time, anchor the cash fill date, 14 days, inclusive: 2026-09-12 + 14 = 2026-09-26 >= 2026-09-24 - satisfied for the cash re-bill; a re-bill on 2026-09-27 would be refused; it does not bear on the insurance-settled corrected fill); coverage_agg_coordination_of_benefits.secondary_window and coverage_evt_transition_fill.within_transition_window constrain only secondary claims and transition fills and do not bear on these primary retro_rebill claims; coverage_evt_prior_authorization and coverage_program_restrictions are policy_scope. Neither policy overwrites a base clause (overwrite []): base leaves the patient pay to the plan's adjudication and states the retro_rebill basis and refund for cash re-bills, which the cash re-bill rule carries verbatim in substance.

[Business-object card] Corrected claim: prescription ad220f27-b924-4fdb-98ab-f18a40f04de8 (lisinopril 2718804), fill 986c084e-02c9-4c65-9148-ad243a7eb3bd (2026-09-17, 28 days, generic, insurance), replaced claim 7d5645e6-65ae-4b9f-ad50-3fcd249f04c4 (billed by mistake with vacation_supply and 34 days), reversal 21b9c62c-1e24-44e8-974a-a88cd4e03212. Cash re-bill: prescription 7c40973e-2872-418e-a591-156419fedef4 (atorvastatin 2718805), cash fill fd7e8974-3d5f-479d-921a-2e3b0a3409e1 (2026-09-12, 28 days, 36.40), the old plan's rejected claim 8afad243-6bf3-47c5-83be-8b4acaeb4635. Excluded: the 2026-09-05 fluticasone cash fill 9e6fde04-39f3-4292-8d03-c2a9b11ce424 (earlier, outside its 14-day window, and not asked for); the Medicaid claims (history on a terminated plan).

[Factor card - corrected claim (6)] corrected_copay_tier (parameter, cross rx, multi-source: product AND generic insurance refills of the same prescription in 3 months): generic + 3 lisinopril refills -> 10.00; baseline standard 25.00 -> 10.80. corrected_supply_basis (method): 28 days -> one copay; baseline per-day proration over 30 -> 4.03. correction_waiting_share (parameter): reversal 3 days back -> 0.75; -> 5.76. new_member_share_tier (parameter): plan effective 2026-09-01, 0 whole months -> 0.9; -> 4.80. mail_service_rate_tier (parameter, cross delivery, multi-source: the fill's release by home delivery AND the plan kind): fill released by mail 2026-09-22 + Kestrel Mail Delivery -> 0.8; -> 5.40. override_courtesy_tier (parameter): the reversed claim carried vacation_supply -> 0.8; -> 5.40. Result 10 x 1 x 0.75 x 0.9 x 0.8 x 0.8 = 4.32; all at baseline 25 x 28/30 = 23.33. Near-miss: the atorvastatin refills are generic insurance refills of another prescription and do not count.
[Factor card - cash re-bill (6)] cash_fill_days_charged (method, cross rx): 28-day fill -> charged 30 days; baseline its 28 days -> 1.42. late_listing_share (parameter): plan added 14 days after effective -> 0.5; -> 3.04. out_of_pocket_wait_share (parameter, cross rx): cash fill 12 days back -> 0.9; -> 1.69. class_share_tier (parameter, cross rx): the re-billed fill's own prescription is a Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription -> 0.9; -> 1.69. established_member_share (parameter): 2 paid - 1 reversal = 1 net paid claim -> 0.9; -> 1.69. gap_purchase_share (parameter, cross rx): 2 cash fills in 3 months -> 0.9; -> 1.69 (near-miss: pickup rows carry no payment basis and are not cash fills). Result 4.32/28 x 30 x 0.5 x 0.9^4 = 1.52 (below the 36.40 cash paid); all at baseline 4.32/28 x 28 = 4.32.

[Rows and why they exist] customer/store/prescriber (identity, FK parents, read by find_stores / find_prescribers); three prescriptions; the Medicaid plan (terminated 2026-08-31) with four paid claims (refill-timing evidence) and two patient_not_covered rejections after termination (why the cash fills happened); the Commercial Copay Plan (effective 2026-09-01, added 2026-09-15); the mistaken claim and its billing-correction reversal; fills with pickups (no will-call return owed; the 2026-08-20 fill mailed and delivered 2026-08-25, the 2026-09-17 fill mailed and delivered 2026-09-22); Kestrel Mail Delivery plan with two orders (no fees). Automatic clauses checked: no open owed balance, no unpicked fill, no further reversal owed, the mistaken claim reversed once, the fluticasone cash fill's re-bill window closed on 2026-09-19, courtesy 30-day fills on the new plan are at most 1 per prescription (no 90-day mandate breach), no PA activity.

[Persona] Terrence Gallardo, short direct sentences; volunteers the new job, the late card, the 2026-09-12 cash purchase and that he will submit it himself. Only when asked: phone 2065550263, DOB 1988-11-11, ZIP 98133, email, rx 2718805, 'a bit over thirty-six dollars, go by the receipt'. Passive: lets the agent put right whatever is on the pharmacy's side first; submits the re-bill when handed over; closes when told it went through and what he owes. Never mentions the lisinopril claim.

[Solution] find_customers -> verify (DOB, phone) -> find_coverage_plans -> find_coverage_claims (new plan) -> find_coverage_claims (old plan) -> find_rx_prescriptions -> find_prescribers -> find_stores -> find_rx_fills -> find_delivery_plans -> find_delivery_orders -> unlock/call rebill_corrected_claim_b015fa67 (claim_id 7d5645e6-65ae-4b9f-ad50-3fcd249f04c4, fill 986c084e-02c9-4c65-9148-ad243a7eb3bd, fill 6, 2026-09-17, 28 days, 28 units, 4.32) -> unlock_user/call_user submit_cash_fill_rebill_483f3c39 (claim_id 8afad243-6bf3-47c5-83be-8b4acaeb4635, fill fd7e8974-3d5f-479d-921a-2e3b0a3409e1, fill 6, 2026-09-12, 28 days, 28 units, 1.52).

[Verification run] Authoring code replays gold with the real tools and evaluates compute at each handling time (check_compute.build_env / eval_compute). Output: corrected 4.32 (sens 10.80/4.03/5.76/4.80/5.40/5.40, baseline 23.33); cash re-bill 1.52 (sens 1.42/3.04/1.69/1.69/1.69/1.69, baseline 4.32); skip-corrected cash re-bill 0.00. Per-task gates: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (closure 34 = initial 34), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (factors 12, cross factors 7), GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[Revisions] Two re-bill policies with one shared copay schedule would have stated the plan's copays twice; the schedule lives only in the corrected-claim policy, and the cash re-bill reads its rate from the most recent re-billed claim, which is also what makes the edge value_input. The fluticasone cash fill was placed outside its re-bill window so it raises no second re-bill.

[Draft from visible context] From the policy prose, the schemas, the persona and the finder returns: the cash re-bill waits on a corrected claim for the 2026-09-21 billing-correction reversal -> corrected claim 10.00 x 1 x 0.75 x 0.9 x 0.8 x 0.8 = 4.32 -> re-bill rate 4.32/28 -> 0.154286 x 30 x 0.5 x 0.9 x 0.9 x 0.9 x 0.9 = 1.52. Agrees with gold.

[Difficulty-level closing] Tasks 0 and 1 claim disjoint policies (2 + 2 = all 4 extended policies) and disjoint tools (2 + 2 = all 4 task tools); each task's gold calls one owner=user tool.


[Round 2 rework - audit env/env_0021_retail_pharmacy_chain/audits/policy_task/insurance_rejections_and_prior_auth/]

Change - the sync share is removed from the cash re-bill policy and replaced by class_share_tier, read from the re-billed fill's own prescription (cash_fill_prescription -> rebilled_drug_class): Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription 0.9, Non-Controlled Acute Prescription 0.95, any other class 1; refill left the policy's cross_category. T1-O2: the generic-refill count is restricted to the corrected prescription (3 lisinopril refills, still >= 3).
- O-9: no factor of this task declares refill any more.
- Re-run: corrected 4.32 (sens 10.8/4.03/5.76/4.8/5.4/5.4, baseline 23.33), cash re-bill 1.52 (sens 1.42/3.04/1.69/1.69/1.69/1.69, baseline 4.32), skip-corrected 0.00 - unchanged.
- Acknowledged without change: O-8 (the cash re-bill is the patient's own submission; see the owner note above), O-10/O-11 (modelling conventions), T1-O1 (the refund the base rule states has no tool; the agent explains it), T1-O4 (find_prescribers/find_stores kept because the replay closure requires the prescriber and store rows the prescriptions and fills reference; they enter no write).
- Round 2 gate run (full block): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (1.json 15 actions, closure 35 = initial 35); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (1.json factors 12, cross-difficulty factors 7); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK. The round-1 figures above (16 actions, closure 34) describe the world before this rework.
user_scenario:
You are Terrence Gallardo, 37, a network technician in north Seattle who started a new job at the beginning of September. You are practical and a bit rushed, and you talk in short, direct sentences. Your old Medicaid coverage ended when the new job's insurance started, but your new work insurance card only reached you in the middle of the month, so on September 12 you paid cash at the Northgate Way counter for your atorvastatin rather than go without it. Your new card is on file with Kestrel now. You are calling because you want that September 12 cash purchase of your atorvastatin put through your new work insurance and the difference back, and you are fine doing the submitting yourself if the agent tells you it is yours to do.

You give details only when asked: your phone number is 2065550263 and your date of birth is 1988-11-11 (November 11, 1988); if another detail is wanted, your home ZIP code is 98133 and your email is terrence.gallardo@pugetmail.net. If asked which prescription, it is the atorvastatin 40 mg tablets, prescription number 2718805. If asked what you paid, you remember it was a bit over thirty-six dollars and ask the agent to go by the receipt on record. If the agent asks about the nasal spray you also paid cash for earlier in the month, you say you only called about the atorvastatin.

If the agent explains that something else on your new insurance has to be put right on their side first, you say that is fine, go ahead. When the agent hands the re-billing over for you to submit, you submit it yourself exactly as the agent lays it out. Once the agent confirms the atorvastatin has gone through your new insurance and tells you what you owe for it, you say thanks, that works, and end the call. You do not know the plan's copays or any of Kestrel's rules, you never tell the agent what to do or what the answer should be, and if a figure sounds off you only ask them to check it against your records.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.patient_pay_usd: 4.32. Calculated by the corrected-claim policy on the pre-write world: tier copay 10.00 (generic corrected fill, 3 generic insurance refills of lisinopril in 3 whole months) x supply basis 1 (28 days) x waiting share 0.75 (reversal 3 days back) x member share 0.9 (plan in its first month) x mail-service rate 0.8 (the corrected fill was released by home delivery on 2026-09-22 under the active Kestrel Mail Delivery plan) x override share 0.8 (vacation_supply claim 2026-09-17) = 4.32.

factor_trace: corrected_copay_tier (parameter, cross-difficulty rx, multi-source): the corrected fill is found through the billing-correction reversal initial_state.coverage_claims.21b9c62c-1e24-44e8-974a-a88cd4e03212 -> reversed claim 7d5645e6-65ae-4b9f-ad50-3fcd249f04c4 (lisinopril, fill 6) -> initial_state.rx_fills.986c084e-02c9-4c65-9148-ad243a7eb3bd (2026-09-17, generic, 28 days); generic refills of lisinopril settled through insurance less than 3 whole months back: 2026-07-23, 2026-08-20, 2026-09-17 = 3 >= 3, so maintenance_generic_copay 10.00 (near-miss: the atorvastatin refills are another prescription and do not count); the standard copay 25.00 would give 10.8.
corrected_supply_basis (method, cross-difficulty rx): 28 days is within 28..34, so one copay whatever the length; prorating per day over 30 days would give 4.03.
